title: Children
definition: Children are gifts from God who bear His image and are to be loved, protected, taught, disciplined, and welcomed with care.
summary: Children have God-given dignity and should be nurtured in truth, love, and protection.
christFocus: Jesus welcomed children and used them to teach humility, dependence, and the nature of receiving the kingdom of God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture treats children as gifts and image-bearers, not interruptions, burdens, or lesser persons. They are to be loved, protected, taught, and guided with patience and care.

Children need instruction in truth and examples of godliness. They also need correction, encouragement, safety, compassion, and prayer. Adults are warned not to despise or harm them.

Jesus welcomed children and showed that they matter in the kingdom of God. Their dependence reminds believers of humility and trust before the Father.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Children are often overlooked, exploited, neglected, or treated as inconvenient. This doctrine matters because it calls God's people to protect and nurture the vulnerable with the heart of Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Value children as image-bearers. Speak to them with dignity, teach them truth, protect them from harm, pray for them, and welcome them as Jesus did.
